answer: Each identity ships in a walnut: a sealed log whose bond is held until the network cracks it at a random epoch. Cracking reveals every job that identity ever did, and two logs that overlap void both copies, so a bought or cloned history self-destructs. Berths are rationed per harbor, and the k-th berth taken in one harbor costs k squared in bond, making a crowded jurisdiction cost about n cubed over three. Every berth carries an ivory serial burned at cracking, so a used identity cannot be resold or rotated into a fresh shell.
